gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many centimetres of ground one thermal pixel covers at the 400 ft ceiling for the Autel EVO Lite 640T or EVO II Dual 640T V3; I could only complete that sum for the two DJI drones, because Autel's pixel pitch could not be opened today (HTTP 429/403).
standout_why: Compared against bestthermaldrone.com/best-thermal-drones, /compare and /learn/thermal-drone-cost, nighthunting.net/thermal-drones and blog.dronetrader.com/thermal-drones-for-sale. bestthermaldrone.com already prints cm per pixel and pixels on a deer or person at 200 ft and 400 ft for the DJI Matrice 4T, DJI Mavic 3 Thermal and Skydio X10, so rivals have part of this. It gives no such figures for either Autel 640T, the two drones Dealectric sells. nighthunting.net says its distances are 'calculated from the sensor and lens' but shows no cm-per-pixel or pixel-on-target value for any model. dronetrader has prices only. None of them states swath width at altitude, average power draw, or the charge-to-flight ratio. My DJI figures are also coarser than bestthermaldrone's (12.1 vs 11.5 cm for the Matrice 4T, 16.1 vs 15.6 cm for the Mavic 3 Thermal).
decides: Sourced today: the EVO II Dual 640T V3 has a 13 mm thermal lens at $4,399 (Rugged Bundle), the EVO Lite 640T a 9.1 mm lens at $3,359, and both are 640 × 512. On the DJI pair the same lens gap means 12.1 cm vs 16.1 cm per pixel at 400 ft, and a 12-pixel deer up to 412 ft vs 311 ft. If Autel's pixel pitch is opened and is the same on both models, the 13 mm EVO II resolves 13/9.1 = 1.43× finer than the EVO Lite and the EVO Lite sees a 1.43× wider strip. That would make the EVO II the pick for spotting animals or people from altitude and the EVO Lite the pick for close roof and solar work and wide sweeps at the lowest price. Until the pitch is sourced, this confirms the direction of the pick but not the Autel centimetre figures.
